title: Game
description: Stage 4 output. A playable game built from a CourseGraph. The model emits content that references the archetype's fixed visual vocabulary by name. It never emits CSS, colours, layout or markup. A game that does not validate against the vocabulary enums is a presentation bug caught before render.

graph_id.description: The CourseGraph this was built from. Quest and Gauntlet built from the same upload share this value: that is the architectural claim, one extraction renders two games.

archetype.description: quest is the narrative arc, long form, teaches. gauntlet is the timed arcade run over the same concepts, short form, verifies.

concept_ids.description: Concepts from the CourseGraph taught in this chapter. Chapter order must respect the prerequisite ordering of these concepts.

background.description: Fixed vocabulary. Hand-built tile sets. Adding one is art work, not a model change.

lines.description: Sets up the concept. Never states the answer to a prediction scene that follows it.

prediction_scene.description: The core mechanic. The learner commits before the reveal, which is the pretesting effect. Distractors come from the CourseGraph misconceptions, never invented here.

prompt.description: Asks the learner to predict an outcome. Must be answerable before instruction, since an unsuccessful attempt is the point.

reveal.description: Shown after the learner commits, whatever they chose. Explains the correct answer and why the tempting wrong one is tempting.

misconception_id.description: Required on every incorrect option. Traces the distractor back to the CourseGraph misconception it came from. This is what makes cohort answer distributions diagnostic rather than decorative: knowing 52 percent picked a specific misconception tells an educator what to reteach.

simulation_scene.description: For concepts at bloom level apply or above. A hand-built widget the learner manipulates. The model chooses the widget and its framing, never implements it.

widget.description: Fixed vocabulary of hand-built widgets, same principle as backgrounds.
